## Question to try and answer/work through and the data with it

How do body mass and flipper length differ among each of the penguin types

Data: [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/),
Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

## Loading and prepping the data

```{python}
#| label: load-python-penguins
#| echo: true
#| warning: false

from palmerpenguins import load_penguins
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import sys

print("Python executable:", sys.executable)

penguins = load_penguins()

penguins_clean = penguins.dropna(
    subset=[
        "species",
        "body_mass_g",
        "flipper_length_mm",
        "bill_length_mm",
        "bill_depth_mm",
    ]
).copy()

penguins_clean.head()
```

## Ploting the body mass and flipper length grouped by each penguin type

```{python}
#| label: fig-python-penguin-size
#| fig-cap: "Body mass and flipper length for the three Palmer Penguin species."
#| echo: true
#| warning: false

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))

colors = {
    "Adelie": "#1f77b4",
    "Chinstrap": "#ff7f0e",
    "Gentoo": "#2ca02c",
}

for species, species_data in penguins_clean.groupby(
    "species",
    observed=True,
):
    ax.scatter(
        species_data["flipper_length_mm"],
        species_data["body_mass_g"],
        label=species,
        color=colors[species],
        alpha=0.7,
    )

ax.set_title("Penguin body mass and flipper length")
ax.set_xlabel("Flipper length (mm)")
ax.set_ylabel("Body mass (g)")
ax.legend(title="Species")
ax.grid(alpha=0.2)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Find the heaviest penguins

```{python}
#| label: python-largest-penguins
#| echo: true

largest_penguins = (
    penguins_clean[
        [
            "species",
            "island",
            "sex",
            "flipper_length_mm",
            "body_mass_g",
        ]
    ]
    .sort_values("body_mass_g", ascending=False)
)

largest_penguins
```

As we can see from the table above,
the heaviest observations are Gentoo penguins as we can see from the
corr. values and the plot we created.
